content: This case centered on a dispute over real estate purchased by a husband during the marriage. The court applied Articles 177 and 179 of the Civil Code to determine if the property was personal or joint. The core interpretive issue was whether the absence of a formal declaration of exclusion under Article 179, paragraph 1, letter f) automatically rendered the asset common property,. The court ruled that if there is objective uncertainty regarding the personal origin of the funds used for the purchase, the lack of a specific declaration results in the asset falling into the legal communion.
